answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns (three per season). Courtship has no player turns; there is no service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use during it.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; courtship is an event, ‘with no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate service (Quarters to Available, then Expended to Quarters); resolve the round-track event; resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; choose an activity tile; invite the exact required gentry; provide all required service; resolve all positive favours before negative favours; optionally buy; clean up by putting all used servants in Expended Service, played gentry in your personal discard, and returning the activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading it as required. The last player advances the marker.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, ‘Hosting an activity’: numbered steps 1–8; it says the event resolves before ongoing effects and specifies each cleanup destination.

answers.answer: Passing order: move all servants directly to Available Service; return all gentry in your discard to hand; resolve the round-track event, then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; the last player advances the marker. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity, not a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.’

answers.answer: Yes. Screening is fixed at the end of step 2, before choosing the activity, so the 6.1 reputation is used for the PR6 tile and guests for this activity, even if the four Service Help actions reduce actual reputation to 3.4 afterward. Each Service Help moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; it cannot take one directly from Expended Service. Service Help is repeatable, subject to having enough reputation to pay.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening: ‘fixed at the end of step 2’ and remains the screening level for the whole activity. Service Help moves one servant ‘from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service’; repeatable and cannot take from Expended Service.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; otherwise their order is your choice. At minimum reputation you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to avoid the loss. A money penalty must be fully payable: use positive money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money; if short, you must borrow if possible, and if you cannot fund it, you cannot play that guest or tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting: ‘Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours.’ Money penalty must be fully payable; ‘You cannot take a negative favour first to shelter it at minimum reputation.’

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gains £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and fully refreshes the Market; this special action is limited to once per turn. At minimum reputation (1.1), you cannot take any special action. Service Help cannot take a servant straight from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table lists costs and limits; text states minimum is 1.1 and ‘at minimum you cannot … take a special action.’

answers.answer: Host the Butler’s Room with an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Hire up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, and put them in Expended Service; there is no money fee. On its upgraded side, instead recruit one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service; unique servants cannot be recruited.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring, ‘Butler’s Room’: activity uses an available butler (or underbutler) and no gentry; hires go to Expended Service; upgraded room recruits one common servant from an opponent’s board.

answers.answer: A housekeeper substitutes for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, a footman substitutes for a valet only when no valets are available. An underbutler may substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, or footman) even while that regular type remains available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: the housekeeper and footman substitutions require that the ordinary type not be available; underbutler may substitute ‘even when that type remains available.’

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take one from the supply immediately into Expended Service. The setup stocks two underbutlers total in Servants for Hire, but Butler’s Room and Hire Servant VP cards cannot hire them. Another player cannot recruit one: the upgraded Butler’s Room recruits only common servants, and unique servants cannot leave their owner’s employ.
answers.evidence: ‘Butler’s Pantry: purchasing it is the only way to acquire an underbutler’; take one from supply into Expended Service. Butler’s Room/VP cards exclude them; upgraded recruitment is for common servants. Setup specifies two underbutlers total.

answers.answer: In the Market, pay the market-space price plus the tile’s printed price modifier. In the Reserve, the base price is £300 plus the modifier. The price cannot be below £100. You cannot buy a duplicate tile you already own; reputation does not restrict purchasing tiles above your reputation.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: Market-space price plus printed modifier; Reserve base £300 plus modifier; minimum £100; never acquire a duplicate; reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space becomes empty, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into the rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile, then draw again; a Reserve-eligible tile goes straight to Reserve, then draw again. If filling multiple spaces, sort only the new tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a duplicate stack leaves the space occupied, so it does not trigger a refill.
answers.evidence: Refill paragraph describes sliding, duplicate stacking and redrawing, Reserve diversion and sorting; it states one tile bought from a two-tile stack leaves an occupied space and causes no refill.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles to Reserve except Largest Wine Cellar; later Service draws also go directly to Reserve except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve, and later PR1 draws go directly there. A full Market refresh after each of the first three courtships is standard: move Reserve-eligible tiles first, leave Reserve unchanged during the refresh, refill all six spaces, then return the set-aside Market tiles to the bag.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve and Refresh: lists the post-courtship 1 Service and post-courtship 2 PR1 moves and later draw rules; full refresh occurs after each of first three courtships and is standard.

answers.answer: At an ordinary courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. Score tile VP in the currently face-up theme category, including negative values; for hybrids, only the face-up category counts. The highest score gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild. If tied for highest, each tied player draws a VP card and nobody gets a Fairchild. Every player discards one secret objective; shuffle the discards and put them on the bottom of the deck. Then open the relevant Reserve, fully refresh the Market, reveal the next theme, pass first-player marker anticlockwise, and advance the round marker.
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep: gives Fairchild return, theme scoring, winner/tie rewards and objective discard; seasonal order ends with passing first-player marker anticlockwise.

answers.answer: At final courtship, return Fairchilds and score tile VP across all four revealed theme cards; a repeated category counts each time, including negative VP. The highest score gets one VP card and a Fairchild. A tie is broken by highest reputation level (wheel position ignored); if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective, then players get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible; move the marker to Wedding Bells and score.
answers.evidence: Final courtship (round 16): specifies all four themes, tie resolution, final objective discard, last chance to use special actions and VP cards, then Wedding Bells and scoring.

answers.answer: End-game VP comes from improvement tiles (printed face-up VP, including negatives and unused tiles); gentry in hand and discard (including family and final Fairchild); fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation; servants (2 VP each); wealth (1 VP per £200, rounded down); and retained unused VP cards (printed VP). Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, and 28 VP. Game tie-break: a tied player with the final Fairchild wins; otherwise highest reputation level wins; if still tied, share victory. Wheel position does not break the tie.
answers.evidence: Final VP table lists all scoring sources and reputation values; victory paragraph gives Fairchild, reputation level, then shared victory.

answers.answer: Normally receive five objectives at setup and two on round 6; discard one at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Additional objectives from Main Library or a VP card increase the retained count but do not add a discard. Simultaneous discards are shuffled together and put face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end, not upgrading them.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: ‘five at setup plus two on round 6’; four courtship discards leave three; simultaneous discards are shuffled; tile objective requires ownership, ‘not upgrading.’

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (multiple cards allowed), and once again after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it to take its benefit; used cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained unused cards score their printed VP, and a card cannot provide both its benefit and final VP.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: describes immediate, later-turn and post-final-courtship use; used cards go to bottom of VP deck; retained cards score printed VP and cannot be used for both.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after its first use; an already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. A hybrid starts with its underlined category icon showing and flips after every use. Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite host their front-side activity once, then upgrade into monuments and cannot host again; their monument benefit starts on later turns. For hybrids, only the currently face-up category counts at courtship and for objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects: normal tiles upgrade after first use; hybrids flip every use; Queen’s and Lionheart Suites upgrade into monuments and can never host again; only face-up hybrid category counts.

answers.answer: Monuments and Servants’ Hall resolve during the ongoing-effects step on hosting turns (after the round event) and on passes (after the round event and before the passing benefit). Monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn, but no income during courtship. Servants’ Hall uses one available servant to reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one reputation yourself; the servant goes to Expended Service at turn end. It may not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Hosting and Passing steps place ongoing effects after the event; Monuments and Servants’ Hall sections specify effects, timing, servant destination and minimum-reputation targeting restriction.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite uses one footman on the tile and one casual guest from hand, with the guest’s normal service; it doubles all that guest’s favours, including negative ones, then upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite uses a housekeeper on the tile and one prestige guest from hand with normal guest service; it doubles one chosen favour and resolves the others normally, then upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite uses a butler on the tile and draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend, with no personal guest service; it doubles nonnegative favours, excludes negative favours from doubling, keeps the guest, and puts it in discard at cleanup; it upgrades into a monument. Each has a fixed count of one guest, which cannot be increased or decreased.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table lists each suite’s tile service, guest source/type and service, favour doubling and later state; following text says all three have a fixed count of one guest that no effect may change.
